text:
B: Hello, can you hear me?
A: Erm, yes. Hi. I'm Kezia.
B: Nikhil. I'm in Thornton Heath. Croydon.
A: Oh, I'm in Catford. So not that far.
B: Not far at all. Two trains, if Southern feels like it. What do you do, Kezia?
A: I'm a teaching assistant. SEN, at a primary in Lewisham. I support two children with autism.
B: Autism. Do you work with the same two all day?
A: Yeah, four days a week. So you get to know them really well. What they like, what upsets them. Like, one of them can't have the hand dryer on. So we take paper towels everywhere.
B: That's a small thing that probably saves a whole afternoon.
A: Yeah. Exactly. What do you do?
B: I'm a CAD technician. Drawings for building services. And I look after two junior technicians, so, er, also two, but much bigger.
A: Ha. Are they okay?
B: They're good. One of them is very fast and doesn't check anything. The other one checks everything three times and is very slow. So I'm trying to make them both a bit more like the middle.
A: I'd be the slow one.
B: Honestly, I prefer the slow one. Slow can be taught to be quicker. Careless is harder.
A: That's sort of nice to hear. In staff meetings I feel like the slow one.
B: Meetings are a different skill. I don't say much in mine either. I just wait and say the one thing that's actually wrong with the drawing.
A: Yeah. I'm like that. I'll think of it on the walk home.
B: Do you walk to work?
A: Thirty-five minutes. It's getting dark in the mornings now, though. I don't like that bit.
B: I cycle to Norwood Junction. Same problem. Lights on at seven. I noticed in your photo your room was very tidy, by the way. I appreciated that.
A: Oh. Thank you. I deep clean on Saturdays. Is that okay, sorry, that's a bit boring.
B: Not boring. My wife would love you. I leave books on every surface. And she's growing chillies in the garden at the moment, so there are pots everywhere too.
A: I've got a peace lily and two spider plants. I keep overwatering the lily.
B: Swati does the opposite, she forgets. Maybe there's a middle there as well.
A: Ha. Yeah. What do you do at weekends, then?
B: Galleries, cooking. Badminton on Thursdays. You?
A: Church, choir. Sunday dinner at my mum's. That's sort of fixed.
B: Fixed is good. What does your mum cook?
A: Erm, rice and peas, chicken. Every week. I batch-cook as well, on Sunday nights, in labelled tubs.
B: Labelled tubs. Of course. I tried making ramen from scratch last weekend and it took eleven hours, and—
